reach.rationale: The app's own code reaches for zero experimental APIs; its exposure is the mandated alpha-state framework baseline plus one recently-stable-but-officially-peer-supported Vite major. That is below the 'one or two experimental APIs in central places' midpoint.

containment.rationale: Framework coupling is confined to server.js, vite.config.ts and ambient.d.ts (the documented integration points); the one undocumented behavior sits behind a single helper module with an explanatory comment, so a framework change would require a one-file fix.

evidence: app/src/routes/(home).ts:2 — server-html html is the documented recommended template import (avoids hydration markers); no stable alternative exists in-framework
app/server.js:14-20 — honoAdapter/getClientBuildPath is the documented Hono integration for server output

app/src/routes/(home).client.ts:1-8 — plain custom elements deliver the spec's debounced search via documented progressive enhancement, avoiding Gracile's 'Experimental. This is not well tested' hydration layer
app/src/lib/build.ts:1-4 — the build-render guard exists solely to satisfy the spec's no-build-time-data-fetch rule
justification.rationale: Every non-long-stable API used is either the framework's documented stable path or required by the spec, and the app consistently chose the least experimental option where the framework offered more adventurous ones (hydration, CSR).

findings.issue: Guards request-time data loading by matching the undocumented 'gracile-static' hostname that Gracile uses for its build-time asset-collection render pass; this sentinel does not appear in the framework docs.
findings.suggestion: Keep the guard but add a fallback (e.g. also treat a missing/aborting handler context as build render), file an upstream request for a documented `context.isBuildRender`/`gracile-static` constant export, and pin the exact Gracile version so the behavior can't drift unnoticed.

findings.issue: The entire app rests on a framework whose own docs banner says 'This project is in an alpha state' (gracile.js.org/docs/), so breaking changes across 0.x minors are the main long-term risk.
findings.suggestion: This is spec-mandated and the app pins ^0.11.0 (patch-only drift for 0.x); consider an exact pin plus a note in the README about the framework's alpha status.

findings.issue: vite ^8.3.5 is a recently-stable major built on the new Rolldown bundler (stable 2026-03-12, ~7.5 months old).
findings.suggestion: Acceptable — @gracile/engine@0.12.0 explicitly declares peer support for '^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0' — but keep an eye on Gracile release notes when bumping either side.

findings.issue: The html import transitively runs on @lit-labs/ssr (labs/experimental channel), confirmed as a dependency of @gracile/gracile@0.11.0 in registry metadata.
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change: this is the framework's documented re-export of the server-only Lit html and the app never imports @lit-labs packages directly.

summary: The app is strikingly conservative for a Gracile project: every framework API it uses (defineRoute handler/document/template, server-html, server output mode, Hono adapter, .client.ts convention, route-template-outlet) is documented in the current stable 0.11.0 release, and it deliberately avoids Gracile's explicitly-experimental hydration and CSR layers in favor of plain custom elements. Its only genuine exposure is ambient (the spec-mandated alpha-state framework and its @lit-labs/ssr underpinning) plus one recently-stable Vite 8 major that Gracile officially peer-supports. The single fragile choice — sniffing the undocumented 'gracile-static' build-render hostname — is well quarantined in an 8-line module but should be replaced with a documented mechanism when one exists.
